guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are slightly less aggressive on Notre Dame than the market, but we still see substantial matchup concerns for Purdue. Notre Dame’s offense has major advantages in rushing efficiency, passing efficiency and scoring-opportunity creation against a defense that grades poorly in each corresponding area. That makes Purdue’s path to staying competitive narrower than the opening result alone might suggest.

We did see encouraging offensive signs from Purdue against Indiana State. The offense produced 523 yards, while Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. That performance matters because Purdue will likely need consistent offensive production to remain within the number, but we are not treating one game as proof—especially with 16 players making their first Purdue starts.

For us, the disagreement comes from giving Purdue’s offensive competence and home-field resistance a little more weight than the market does. The concern is that Notre Dame’s underlying offensive advantages are broad enough to create separation anyway. Our view differs from the market, but not by enough to justify a wager at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
The matchup we are watching is Notre Dame’s rushing offense against Purdue’s run defense. Purdue held Indiana State to 66 rushing yards, but our longer-run metrics still place this defense near the bottom nationally in rush EPA while Notre Dame’s offense ranks near the top.

We think that contrast will tell us whether the opener reflected meaningful defensive improvement or simply a favorable single-game result. If Purdue cannot prevent efficient rushing gains, Notre Dame should have repeated chances to create scoring opportunities, which is the clearest threat to Purdue staying inside the number.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State.
Purdue produced 523 yards of total offense against Indiana State, its first 500-yard game since Oct. 12, 2024 at Illinois.
Purdue allowed Indiana State 284 total yards, including 66 rushing yards, and 12 first downs.
Sixteen players made their first Purdue starts and 38 players made their Purdue debuts in the season opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue is scheduled to host Notre Dame for the Shillelagh Trophy on Sept. 26, 2026.
The guide lists Notre Dame as No. 4 with a 1-0 record at the time of publication.
Purdue lost 56-30 to Notre Dame in 2025, Barry Odom's only previous meeting with Notre Dame as Purdue's head coach.

quarterback.fact: Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions against Indiana State.
Browne's season opener was his fourth career 300-yard passing game and his 15th career start for Purdue.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and threw for 2,153 yards and nine touchdowns.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed for the backup quarterback role; Meredith previously started against Northwestern in 2023 but did not play during the next two seasons.

offensive_personnel.fact: True freshman Brock Brownfield became Purdue's first true freshman offensive lineman to start a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona was the only returning offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey appeared in 11 games.
Purdue added offensive-line transfers Boaz Stanley, Nuku Mafi and Micah Banuelos, who entered the season with 21, 12 and five career starts, respectively.
Minnesota transfer Fame Ijeboi led Purdue against Indiana State with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and added two receptions for 30 yards.
FAU transfer Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut.
Xavier Townsend caught seven passes for 47 yards and returned three punts for 24 yards in his Purdue debut.
Devin Mockobee graduated after leading Purdue in rushing four times and finishing fourth in program history with 2,987 career rushing yards.

defensive_personnel.fact: FIU transfer Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup in his Purdue debut.
Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown against Indiana State, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.
Linebacker Charles Correa returned after starting all 12 games in 2025 and recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks.
Purdue added defensive-line transfers Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought 81 combined games of college experience.
New defensive-back starters in the opener included Jaden Mangham, Mister Clark, John Slaughter and Don Saunders.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Zach Crabtree became Purdue's offensive line coach after coaching at Fresno State in 2025.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach during the offseason.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and is expected to miss the 2026 season.
Tight end George Burhenn returned against Indiana State after 349 days without game action and caught two passes for 43 yards.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned after missing the 2025 season because of injuries.
Magwood caught a six-yard touchdown against Indiana State, his first touchdown since 2022.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue's season-opening offense totaled 346 passing yards and 177 rushing yards.
Purdue did not commit a turnover against Indiana State.
Five different players scored Purdue touchdowns against Indiana State, and each recorded his first points as a Boilermaker.
Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen for 2026, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue recorded eight tackles for loss and three sacks against Indiana State.
Purdue held Indiana State to 66 rushing yards.
The Boilermakers forced one turnover against Indiana State, with Don Saunders returning the interception for a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts and all five extra points against Indiana State.
Echeverria Lozano's field goals came from 39, 27 and 25 yards, giving him the most field goals in a game by a Purdue freshman since at least 1995.
Buffalo transfer Dylan Drennan punted once for 54 yards with a 49-yard net in his Purdue debut.

series_context.fact: Notre Dame leads the Purdue series 61-26-2 and has won 10 consecutive meetings.

other_relevant.fact: Purdue was 1-0 when this Game 2 guide was published, so it does not include results from the intervening Wake Forest and UCLA games before the scheduled Notre Dame matchup.
